title: Hikmat and the Unlit Room
logline: Hikmat descends into Salma and learns the dark was only unremembered light.
story: Everyone warned that Salma, who was silent wisdom weaver, could not be reached — the way down was made of everything Hikmat had refused to remember. Hikmat, who carried wisdom, went looking anyway. So instead of fighting the dark, Hikmat sat in it and listened — and the dark, for the first time, was not afraid of being seen. When Hikmat rose, nothing outside had changed, and everything had. The darkness had not been an enemy; it was only a room with the light switched off, waiting for someone unhurried enough to find the switch within.
moral: The darkness is not the absence of light, but light that has not yet been remembered.
attribution: a Pagarek parable, from Project Genesis
